proposed_fixes.title: Isolate the nonclient-input fail-fast before changing Settings
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the affected WinUI runtime or its nonclient input integration fails during move/resize in the standard-user environment. The module signature supports this boundary, but does not identify the faulty call or prove a PowerToys defect.
plan: Compare a current failing Event Viewer signature with the supplied 0.74/0.79 Microsoft.UI.Input fail-fast before treating later Settings startup exceptions as the same bug.
Reproduce standard-user versus elevated move/resize with the same installed runtime, then trace Settings and File Locksmith window/input initialization.

Only if that trace identifies invalid PowerToys input-object lifetime or initialization ordering, correct the shared initialization/teardown boundary and add a regression case; otherwise route the signature to the runtime owner.
verification: Move, resize, refocus and open flyouts repeatedly as a standard user and elevated user; verify Settings and File Locksmith remain usable without changing unrelated security policy.
Verify the original affected installation no longer produces the same fail-fast signature.

confidence.rationale: The failing module is known but no stack establishes the PowerToys call site; reinstall recovery and the elevation difference leave competing causes.

known_information: Versions 0.74 and 0.79 are represented in the discussion.
Diagnostic ZIPs, Event Viewer records and a one-monitor comparison were already supplied.
A single-monitor reboot did not resolve the second contributor's failure; administrator mode did.
The issue remains open, is labeled Issue-Bug and has no assignees.
inferences: A runtime/input integration or installation/environment interaction is plausible; a monitor-count-only cause is weakened by the supplied comparison.
The original reporter's recovery does not establish that every contributor's installation is fixed.

comment.body:
Thank you for the existing attachments, Microsoft.UI.Input.dll / 0xc0000602 records, and the single-monitor and administrator comparisons. The original reporter later said a clean reinstall solved their case, but the other affected installation's status is unclear.

1. Could an affected contributor confirm whether Settings still crashes when moved or resized as a standard user, and provide the installed PowerToys version?
2. If it still crashes, please open Event Viewer > Windows Logs > Application immediately afterward and copy the PowerToys.Settings.exe error's faulting module, exception code and version fields, omitting personal paths. This distinguishes the same input failure from a different startup crash.

There is no need to resend the historical ZIPs or repeat the single-monitor test.
